name: new.target is inherited by arrows and works with recursion
source: function G(n: number): number { const kind = () => (new.target === undefined ? 1 : 2); if (n > 0) { return kind() * 10 + n + G(n - 1); } return kind(); } function H(n: number): void { if (n > 0) { new H(n - 1); } console.log(n, new.target ? "new" : "call"); } function main(): void { console.log(G(2)); new G(2); H(1); new H(1); }
